messages:
DeployBot: INCIDENT: High-severity alert — Datadog ingest delay detected for metrics and traces in us-west-2. Paging oncall now. Details: multiple API 5xxs from datadog-ingest, backlog growing.
Sam (oncall SRE): I’m on it. Acknowledged.
Sam (oncall SRE): First quick check — are internal metrics showing traffic spike or is it purely observability?
Lena (Observability): We’re seeing normal traffic on prod frontend, but our Datadog forwarders are returning 502s and ingestion queue length increased ~45m ago. Logs from forwarder show: `error: upstream service error 502` and repeated `http request failed` entries.
Sam (oncall SRE): Thanks. Opening an incident bridge. Short-term plan: 1) Triage whether this is Datadog API or our forwarders saturating. 2) If Datadog is degraded, enable fallback telemetry sinks (CloudWatch / internal TSDB) for critical alerts and heartbeat metrics. 3) Coordinate CS to inform any customers with SLOs tied to alerting.
Clara (PM): Noted. We have a customer on APM SLA mid-migration — PM flagged that alerts might miss. Need a quick customer impact assessment.
Mika (Support): I’ll start a query for any support tickets since the window opened and flag customers with active alerting.
Sam (oncall SRE): Command checks: listing forwarder errors and recent 5xxs.```bash
kubectl -n observability logs deploy/datadog-forwarder --since=60m | grep -i "502\\|5.."
```
Raj (Infra): Forwarders have been restarted once automatically by k8s; pod restarts at ~2050001000 but errors persisted after restart. Network path to datadog endpoints looks healthy from our egress hosts (tcp handshakes ok).
Lena (Observability): Datadog status page shows degraded ingest for that region: https://status.datadoghq.com/incidents/xxxx (note: link updated). They’re reporting backlog and elevated API error rates.
DeployBot: System note — incident created: INC-2050003210. Bridge: #incident-2050003210.
Sam (oncall SRE): Given datadog status, pivot to mitigations: 1) Turn off non-essential telemetry to reduce backlog. 2) Fan-out key heartbeats/traces to CloudWatch (short-term). 3) Increase local retention for logs to avoid loss. I’ll run the fan-out script.
Sam (oncall SRE): Running fan-out:```bash
/scripts/telemetry/fanout_to_cloudwatch --selectors "service:frontend OR metric:cpu*" --dry-run
```
Sam (oncall SRE): Dry-run looks good. Proceeding with live fan-out now.
Lena (Observability): I’m creating temporary CloudWatch dashboards for critical SLOs and wiring up basic alerts to PagerDuty. Copying queries over now. Will post links when done.
Priya (Customer Success): Which customers are likely affected? I have a list of high-SLA customers and one enterprise customer had a deployment today. Need to know if we should proactively notify.
Mika (Support): Found two customers that opened support incidents at ~2050002900 mentioning missing alerts. I’ve escalated both to Priority.
Clara (PM): Please add product-impact flags if any alerting or APM traces are missing — we need to know margin for SLA windows.
Sam (oncall SRE): Quick detection check: are our internal synthetic canaries missing?
ConsoleBot: Synthetic runner: last healthy run 2050002700, next run failed to report at 2050003205 (timeout).
Sam (oncall SRE): That aligns with when Datadog started returning errors. So observability blindspot exists for ~20–40m window.
Lena (Observability): Implemented CloudWatch metrics and created minimal dashboards. I also pushed a mitigation to increase local log retention on the forwarder side: `kubectl patch cm forwarder-config --patch '{"data":{"local_retention":"72h"}}'`.
Sam (oncall SRE): Rolling update to forwarders to pick up config.```bash
kubectl rollout restart deploy/datadog-forwarder -n observability
```
Raj (Infra): Noted — k8s rollout started. I’ll monitor egress rate to datadog to avoid exacerbating backpressure.
Mika (Support): Reached out to affected customer #42 (enterprise) with an initial note: "We’re investigating intermittent observability gaps; we’ll update shortly." Customer replied asking for ETA — no SLA breach reported yet.
Priya (Customer Success): I’ll prepare a proactive email template for impacted customers and include the temporary fallback to CloudWatch for critical alerts.
Sam (oncall SRE): Next: open a support ticket with Datadog with our ingestion logs and sample error traces. Include request for ETA and backlog size. Lena, can you attach the forwarder logs?
Lena (Observability): Attached logs to the ticket and included example payloads showing 502s and rate-limiting responses (`429`). Ticket ID: DD-2050003210-1.
Clara (PM): How long do we expect the blindspot to persist? Can we estimate recovered signal once Datadog resolves backlog?
Sam (oncall SRE): From past incidents, once Datadog marks ingest recovered we’ll see backlog drain over 30–90m depending on queue lengths. Meanwhile we keep critical traces in CloudWatch for immediate alerting.
DeployBot: Update: Datadog status page now shows "Partial recovery" for ingest in us-west-2.
Lena (Observability): Datadog reports they’ve cleared some backlog and are accepting requests again. I’m switching the fan-out back to dry-run to avoid duplicate ingestion.
Sam (oncall SRE): Transition plan: 1) Stop further fan-out to avoid duplicate billing/ingest; 2) Let Datadog drain backlog; 3) Keep CloudWatch dashboards live for an hour and then fold them into a postmortem artifact.
Raj (Infra): Back-pressure metrics show queues shrinking after ~30m post-recovery — good sign.
Mika (Support): Customer #42 confirmed no missed alerts after we rerouted critical ones and appreciated the proactive message.
Priya (Customer Success): Closing loop: I sent personalized notes to the two affected customers and offered follow-up postmortem.
Clara (PM): Can we add a short-term playbook item to avoid full loss next time? Maybe automatic fan-out for critical metrics when third-party ingress is degraded.
Sam (oncall SRE): Agreed. I’ll file an action item: implement automatic fan-out and a toggle to dedupe once primary recovers.
Lena (Observability): Adding to obs backlog: auto-fanout, dedupe logic, and better forwarder health alerts (alarm when forwarder returns > 5xx for > 5m).
Sam (oncall SRE): For the incident timeline: root cause is Datadog ingest partial outage. Impact: observability blindspot for ~20–50m affecting synthetic checks, metrics/trace ingestion; no production feature regressions. Mitigation: fan-out to CloudWatch, increased local retention, customer notifications.
Clara (PM): Thank you team. Please capture timeline and artifact links in the incident doc. Assign postmortem owner.
Sam (oncall SRE): I’ll own the postmortem. Adding notes and artifacts now.
DeployBot: Incident INC-2050003210 status: RESOLVED — monitoring for any regressions.
Sam (oncall SRE): Closing bridge. If you see anything odd, @Sam (oncall SRE) — ping me. :thumbsup:
Lena (Observability): Leaving a quick note: we should also test the dedupe flow end-to-end before enabling automatic fan-out.
Priya (Customer Success): Thanks everyone, nice work coordinating.
Mika (Support): Will mark the support tickets with incident reference and follow up tomorrow.
Clara (PM): Postmortem owner: Sam. Timeline doc: https://redwood-internal/incident/2050003210/postmortem (will be filled out).
Sam (oncall SRE): End of thread — archiving notes to incident doc and scheduling a short retro.
